html:
Democrats have secured a sweeping victory in the US midterm elections, regaining full control of both chambers of Congress and delivering a historic defeat to Republicans and Donald Trump. This significant political shift is largely attributed to voter dissatisfaction with the ongoing war in Iran and domestic economic concerns, signaling potential widespread reverberations for global affairs.

US Midterms Aftermath: The Democratic Party's "blue wave" resulted in the capture of both the House and Senate, marking the first time they have held full control of Congress since 2023. Donald Trump acknowledged the Republican defeat, which included historic losses across the country, while downplaying his own role and celebrating his team; however, reports indicate a decline in his wealth. Several sources attribute the Democratic success partly to public disapproval of the war in Iran and high-level corruption. Abdul El-Sayed also made history as the first Muslim elected to the US Senate.

Iran War: The ongoing conflict with Iran was a central theme influencing US voters, with Trump stating the war was "worth it" despite its impact on Republican losses. Iran has celebrated the Republican defeat, interpreting it as a "no to war" message from Americans, though its Supreme Leader warns against expecting a change in US "hostility." US strikes were reportedly carried out on Iran's Qeshm Island, while Iran declared a US ceasefire proposal "insufficient," warning that any confrontation could extend to Europe. Oil prices plummeted significantly amid hopes for an end to the conflict.

Russia-Ukraine and Global Security: In Ukraine, Kyiv reports that a Russian "double-tap bombing" killed at least 40 people, with dozens more potentially under rubble, as Russia launched a massive barrage of drones and missiles across nine regions. Despite this, a short ceasefire in the Kherson region provided residents with a momentary return to normal life. Separately, the Indian navy rescued 20 crew from an Iranian fishing boat hijacked off Somalia, highlighting a resurgence of piracy in the Gulf of Aden. North Korea also tested a ballistic missile with a cluster warhead.

Middle East Dynamics: In Israel, President Herzog has begun consultations after an election deadlock, urging politicians to avoid another election, and accepted certified results despite Netanyahu's claims of vote fraud. Trump announced the US would cease $4 billion in annual military aid to Israel starting at the end of 2026, a move Netanyahu reportedly concealed from Israeli voters. Meanwhile, Israeli forces conducted raids in Jenin, detaining Palestinians, while colonists seized homes and attacked activists in the West Bank.

European Developments: French blood storage facilities were impacted by freezer hacks, with theories swirling about culprits. In Serbia, nine active and one former police officer were detained for allegedly using excessive force against anti-corruption protesters last year. Hungary released Communist-era secret service files 37 years after the fall of communism, a move criticized as too late and incomplete. The UK government is also considering a ban on smart glasses due to concerns over surreptitious filming.

Global Economy & Trade: With US-Canada trade talks resuming, Canadians are hopeful for tariff relief following the Democratic wave. Leading figures in the Caribbean reparatory justice movement have rejected the UK's offers of debt relief and aid as replacements for reparations for slavery, following UK PM Andy Burnham's announcement on dialogue and apology but ruling out reparations.
